entry.title: Diptych with Twelve Apostles & St. Paul
entry.by: Workshop or Circle of Wäldä Maryam
entry.blurb: Depicting 13 holy men, this diptych (two-panel painting) is sized for an Ethiopian Orthodox Christian church or elite home.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund

facts: It is painted in the bold, colorful style associated with royal court workshops from the early 1600s to the mid-1700s.
Captions in Ge’ez––an eastern African language dating to the 400s BCE––identify each by name.
This African language is nearly 2,500 years old!

candidate.title: Diptych with Twelve Apostles & St. Paul
candidate.maker: Workshop or Circle of Wäldä Maryam
candidate.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund
candidate.description: Depicting 13 holy men, this diptych (two-panel painting) is sized for an Ethiopian Orthodox Christian church or elite home. It is painted in the bold, colorful style associated with royal court workshops from the early 1600s to the mid-1700s. Painter Wäldä Maryam (or someone he trained) set this scene of Christ’s apostles in the context of his homeland. Each saint wears fashionable clothing imported from India. While they are posed and dressed similarly to emphasize their group identity, the artist portrayed their faces and hairstyles individually. Captions in Ge’ez––an eastern African language dating to the 400s BCE––identify each by name. Captions written in the language Gəˁəz identify each holy man by name. This African language is nearly 2,500 years old!
candidate.culture: Africa, East Africa, Ethiopia, presumably Gondär
